mission_03: Neuromorphic computing mimics the brain's event-driven, sparse computation using spiking neurons. The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) model is the simplest spiking neuron: it integrates incoming currents (leaky integration: V(t+1) = leak * V(t) + input), fires a spike when the membrane potential exceeds a threshold, then resets and enters a refractory period. Unlike traditional neural networks that compute at every timestep, spiking neurons only communicate when they fire, making them extremely energy-efficient. In this mission, you implement the LIF neuron model with leak, threshold, reset, and refractory period, compose them into a spiking neural network with weighted synaptic connections, process spike trains through the network timestep by timestep, and decode outputs using rate coding (counting spikes per neuron).
